name: David Adegbola
title: Forestry student with a computing background
headline: I study forest bioeconomy at UEF and came to forestry from computing, so I'm useful in the field and at the keyboard.
statements: Computing first: an OND in Computer Science (Ibadan, 2019–2022), then IT studies at VAMK.
A fitter's job at UPM Kaukas in 2025 showed me the forest industry from the inside. Employer rating: excellent.
Now at UEF: tree measurement and soil sampling on field courses, GIS next.

contact.heading: Hiring for forestry, research or technical work?
contact.text: I'm looking for forestry trainee and field work, research assistant roles and technical jobs.

description: David Adegbola: Sustainable Forest Bioeconomy student at UEF with a computing background, looking for forestry, research assistant and technical work in Finland.
about: At the mill I watched logs float on Lake Saimaa and started asking where they came from and how the forests behind them are managed. That question is why I study forestry now.
The computing came first, so I'm at home on the technical side too: Linux, a C program reading a real sensor, and small web services that run on their own.
offer: Field work: measuring, sampling and recording to a checklist, outdoors in any weather, by the site's safety rules.
Research projects: collecting data the same way every time, and handling the computing side of it.
Technical work: hardware, networks, user accounts and web services such as domains and email routing.
softwareNote: For my own software I use an AI coding agent (Claude Code): I write the spec and check the result.
learningNote: GIS and remote sensing are what I'm learning now. These are planned or unfinished, not done yet.
